newsitem.title: USA: Sears, Roebuck named in shareholder lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Sears, Roebuck named in shareholder lawsuit.

text.p: A class action lawsuit was filed in Chicago against Sears, Roebuck and Co alleging the retailer and three officers misled investors by failing to disclose a credit card business practice which violated federal bankruptcy law, attorneys who filed the lawsuit said Monday.

The lawsuit revolves around Sears' admission earlier this month that it did not properly file with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court some agreements to continue receiving payments from bankrupt holders of Sears' credit cards.
Sears said it will pay back millions of dollars in debt collected under the agreements and would also issue $100 gift certificates to card holders affected.
Last week, the U.S. Attorney's office in Massachusetts filed a civil lawsuit against the company to stop the allegedly "fraudulent" debt collection activities.
The latest lawsuit, filed in U.S. District Court in Chicago, names as defendants Sears, chief exectuive officer Arthur Martinez, chief financial officer Alan Lacy and controller James Blanda.
Sears also faces a continuing federal investigation in the matter, lawsuits by debtors and others by shareholders, and possible punitive damages in bankruptcy court.
Sears said last week it was cooperating with the probe by federal prosecutors.
